title: Polynomial-time unary remainder
statement: Let $f$ assign a natural number to every bit string, and suppose the function that maps $x$ to the unary word consisting of $f(x)$ true bits is polynomial-time computable. For every natural number $k$, the function that maps $x$ to the unary word consisting of $f(x)\bmod k$ true bits is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: Unary encoding of $f$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If a unary value is polynomial-time computable, then for every fixed constant the unary word of its remainder is polynomial-time computable, by native subtraction after the finite-control quotient scan; the zero-constant case is included.
